title: ‘No publicist or manager in sight’: 80s Madonna, unseen and off-duty – in pictures
text:
‘No publicist or manager in sight’: Madonna in the 80s, unseen and off-duty – in pictures
In Madonna Into the Groove: An Intimate Portrait of the Queen of Pop, photographer Ken Regan opens his archive from 1985 to show never-before-seen photographs of the musician. The 160-page hardback showcases Madonna at her most vibrant, captured on a February day in Los Angeles, with accompanying biographical text by journalist Tomás Mier. With the majority of images previously unpublished, the book is a behind-the-scenes look at an artist coming into the peak of her powers
Madonna at the Le Mondrian hotel gym, Los Angeles, 1985. Photograph: Ken Regan
In 1985, Madonna’s first imperial phase was in full swing, with her Like a Virgin single and album both hitting No 1 in the US and her budding romance with Sean Penn splashed on the front page of global tabloids. People wanted to know all about the Madonna-Penn romance, and People wanted to give it to them,’ writes author Tomás Mier in Madonna: Into the GroovePhotograph: Ken Regan
‘I was surprised People was putting Madonna on the cover,’ photographer Ken Regan later recalled. ‘I didn’t think she warranted it.’ His mind would soon changePhotograph: Ken Regan
‘Madonna loved the camera, and the feeling was mutual,’ Regan wrote in his book All Access. ‘She knew her own sexuality, and she knew exactly how to look and how to pose. I barely had to tell her anything. Madonna was wed to the camera’Photograph: Ken Regan
‘In her hotel room, Madonna and Regan spent about three hours shooting,’ writes Mier. ‘With no publicist or manager in sight, she embraced his vision’Photograph: Ken Regan
‘People have tried to recreate that image, and it doesn’t really work,’ Regan’s daughter Suzanne says. ‘She’s touching the mirror like she’s reaching out to herself’Photograph: Ken Regan
‘In line with the Healthy Swimmer theme of the Red Ballroom setup, Regan and Madonna extended their session into Le Mondrian’s gym. ‘She was even willing to work out on all of the exercise machines in the hotel gym,’ Regan wrotePhotograph: Ken Regan
